narrative:
The decision regarding your law school application was influenced by a prediction indicating an 87% likelihood that you would fail the bar exam if you were to take it. This high probability of failure is a significant concern for admissions committees, as passing the bar is essential for a successful legal career.

The primary factors contributing to this prediction were your academic performance in your first and third years, as well as your current work status. Your grades placed you in the lower decile compared to accepted students, particularly in your third year, where the average performance of admitted students was notably higher. This suggests that your academic trajectory may not have been strong enough to indicate readiness for the challenges of the bar exam.

Additionally, your LSAT score was below the average of accepted applicants, which is another critical indicator of potential success in law school and on the bar exam. Lastly, your part-time work status, while common, may have also played a role in the model's assessment, as most successful candidates tend to work full-time, allowing them to focus more on their studies.

Given this feedback, it would be beneficial for you to consider strategies to strengthen your academic profile. This could include retaking courses to improve your grades, preparing more thoroughly for the LSAT, or gaining relevant experience in a full-time capacity. These steps could enhance your future applications and better position you for success in law school and beyond.
